assign.request: At 400px a page title that is one long word breaks mid-word (Documentatio / n on /websites/tag/documentation/). Fix the cause once in Page.css inside its layer without changing the h1 at 1280+.
steps: pick the fix (shrink floor vs hyphens) and write the CSS
one line in readme or doc

log.msg: Reproduced not on the brief's tag page (documentation lowercase, 13 chars, fits at 400) but on /websites/python-docs-index/ - title 3.14.7 Documentation, matches critic-websites' own logged finding. before.jpg: Documentatio / n split across two lines at 400x844.

Root cause: lew42.css sets .theme-lew42 :is(h1,.h1) { font-size: 3em } (theme layer, specificity 0,2,0) with no clamp; framework.css base layer's overflow-wrap: break-word then breaks the oversized word as a last resort. Nothing in Page.css governed h1 size before this fix.

Fix: Page.css, .page h1.page-title { font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 9vw, 3em) }. Specificity (0,2,1) beats lew42's (0,2,0) in the same theme layer regardless of load order. Max branch is the identical 3em expression, so it's a no-op above the ~460px crossover where 9vw first exceeds it - proven pixel-identical on /framework/'s h1 at 1920 (rect x323.1875 y48 w640 h105.59375, both before and after, plus fontSize 48px unchanged on python-docs-index's own h1.page-title at 1920).
after.jpg at 400x844 on python-docs-index: Documentation now whole on its own line, font-size 36px (was 42px), height 118.8px (was 138.6px, one fewer wrapped line).

Considered hyphens: auto (lang=en is set on <html>) instead - rejected because it still SPLITS the word (with a hyphen), where the brief asks to keep it whole; shrinking is the only option that never breaks the word.

assign.now: readme line written, running documentation skill

assign.outcome:
**One rule, in Page.css, fixes the mid-word title break.** The bug wasn't on the brief's tag page (`documentation` alone fits at 400) but where `critic-websites` actually found it: [`/websites/python-docs-index/`](/websites/python-docs-index/), title `3.14.7 Documentation` — the theme's flat `h1 { font-size: 3em }` (`lew42.css`) has no clamp, so at 400 the word `Documentation` is wider than the column and framework.css's base-layer `overflow-wrap: break-word` breaks it mid-letter as a last resort.

`.page h1.page-title { font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 9vw, 3em) }` — the max branch is the theme's own `3em` expression, so above the ~460px crossover it's a no-op; (0,2,1) beats the theme rule's (0,2,0) in the same `theme` layer on specificity, not load order. Shrinking was chosen over `hyphens: auto` (`<html lang="en">` is set) because hyphens still SPLITS the word — the brief asked to keep it whole.

![before: Documentatio / n split across two lines at 400](before.jpg) ![after: Documentation whole on one line at 400](after.jpg)

**1920 h1 rect, `/framework/` (unrelated to `.page-title`, so it proves the rule doesn't leak) — pixel-identical before and after:** x 323.1875, y 48, w 640, h 105.59375, fontSize 48px, both runs. python-docs-index's own `h1.page-title` also unchanged at 1920: fontSize 48px = 3em, the clamp's max branch.
